who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane claims lints, fix-hello-1113
where: doc comments across crates/ ("never panics", "allocates nothing", "is thread-safe", "guarantees"); crates/blaze-lints/src/blaze/claims/; scripts/src/bin/invariants.rs
what: Doc comments state promises (effects, ordering, bounds) that nothing ties to a proof: a reader, an agent above all, takes them as fact. A keyword search for promise words found about 21 whole-item promises in 40 sampled lines (53%); the rest were qualified ("a warm read allocates nothing") or about something else, so a lint keyed on words alone is wrong half the time.
cost: a stale or false promise is believed until someone reads the code under it; an effect sentence the effect walk would prove is a sentence nobody checks
cause: rustdoc gives a promise no form a tool can read, so a held claim and a hope look the same
class: a statement of fact in prose with no pointer to what makes it true
prevention: one form per held claim (an attribute the build checks, or a `# Guarantees` / `# Invariants` item ending in `Evidence:` or `Unverified:`), the six claim lints, and the ledger in invariants.rs that counts open claims per crate and refuses a level going down
workaround: read an effect sentence only in the narrow form (a clause that opens with the phrase and ends with it); write any other promise as a `# Guarantees` item
